newsitem.title: USA: US defense chief says job pressure led him to quit.
newsitem.headline: US defense chief says job pressure led him to quit.

text.p: Defence Secretary William Perry said on Wednesday the constant pressure of sending U.S. troops into dangerous situations where some could be killed was a key reason why he was leaving the Pentagon.

Speaking at a business conference in San Francisco, Perry gave the fullest account yet of why he has decided to step down as secretary of defence and not to stay on in the high-profile post during President Bill Clinton's second term.
Asked by an audience member why he was leaving, Perry said he had been reluctant to take the job in the first place.
"In fact, I turned the president down the first time he asked me," Perry, 69, told hundreds of people at a technology conference sponsored by Business Week.

"It's a damn tough job. It's enormous pressures, it's not just the pressures of managing a big enterprise, which it is -- more than three million people, more than $250 billion a year budget. But there's something unique about this job which, until you've had it, you cannot appreciate it," he said.

"And that is, every week I sign deployment orders which send our soldiers, sailors, airmen and marines out to situations in which their lives are at risk. And some of these weeks, some of those soldiers I send out there lose their lives and I have to tell their families about it, meet with them," he said in a hushed and emotional voice.

"This aspect of the job, which is dealing with the use of military force, the risks that our troops face every time they go on a mission ... this pressure wears on you and four years is about as long as I think anybody can take it," he said.
Peacekeeping missions, as well as combat missions, involved risks, said Perry, who has just returned from a week-long trip to the Mediterranean, Bosnia, the Arabian peninsula and Japan.

Perry said that "in the entire history of the job of secretary of defence, no one has ever succeeded in serving two full terms. Two secretaries have tried to do it and did not finish the second term."
Perry served for a year as deputy defence secretary under the late Les Aspin and has been secretary almost three years. He also served as an assistant secretary in the Carter administration.

Perry has told Clinton that he will leave the Pentagon as soon as a successor is named. He is expected to return to northern California early next year to resume teaching at Stanford University, where he used to teach mathematics.
In his speech to the conference, Perry stressed the importance of digital technology which he said was beginning to change the way the military fights and deters wars.
